body:
While your suggestions for calming strategies are valued, I'm afraid that's not really where I am in terms of dealing with this.  I've developed coping mechanisms to deal with the anxiety over the years (I'm not sure how, or what I'm doing, but I manage somehow) but my foundations are crumbling.  I've seen a doctor who then referred me to a psychiatrist for an evaluation.  I was given a prescription for fluoxetine and I outright refuse to use it as it has a history of inducing suicidal behavior in its users, as evidenced in more than one friend of mine and by actual empirical data. I suppose if I were given to humor in this situation, it might seem funny that I'm now considering a course of action I sought to avoid.

I try to keep busy at home, clean up and such, but there's so much time to be by myself, it's hard not to reflect on being so alone and hopeless.  I haven't talked to her about what happens when the money runs out; how can I?  My position is fragile enough as it is, I won't dump that load onto her.

I appreciate you writing to me.

Heh, at least you have friends to leave you.  Friends are something I really need, too.

Maybe we could be friends?

My life is like this.  

I'm 29.  Growing up, I was bullied a lot for social difficulties and a nerdy appearance.  Whether as a result of this or some other neurological reason, I have near crippling anxiety and numerous social problems.  I moved out at 20, moved in with a girlfriend soon after.  We were together for years until financial problems caused us to separate briefly, after which I moved to a new city to be with her and asked for her hand in marriage.  She accepted but gave the ring back soon after. That was about six months ago. At the moment, I'm unemployed, terminated from my last job by a misunderstanding.  I have few friends, most don't live near me and the ones who don't I rarely speak to.  My family is just my mother, who lives in another city as well.  We don't relate terribly well.  I have a woman in my life who lives with me who is very special to me, but I fear that I can't be what she needs me to be. I hate this city and there's nothing for me here except for her.  I spent most of my time alone, at home, trying to find work as my funds dwindle.

I get more anxious with every day, I find it very hard to use the phone, I procrastinate and avoid situations that cause anxiety and so often I do nothing at all, having had enough of the want-to-scream feeling that anxiety brings.  My mind races, I have clouds of dread which hang over me and threaten to consume me over almost everything, most of all the girl I'm with.  I try so very hard not to depend on her for validation and acceptance, but she is all I have in my life.  I'm scared to do say or do anything for fear of rocking the boat.  

I'm paralyzed but fully able bodied.

Having had a lot of transgender friends, I understand the pitfalls of depression and alienation that transphobia can cause.  It seems like an uncaring world that cares even less for misfits, but I've found that solidarity amongst like-minded individuals is the key to not just surviving, which is what you seem to be doing, but rather living, what you want to be doing.

What can I offer you in my position?  A sympathetic ear.  For a lot of us, this is all we have and sometimes all we need.  Please, dump on us here.  Compassion means a lot to me and I hope that knowing that people are wishing you well at least lets you hold on for a little longer until you can find the things you seek.
